artifacts.summary: Inventories every instruction surface under agent-system/extensions/sapience/**, finds most of deliverable (a) already implemented by a prior task, identifies two stale domain-doc passages still describing the old untagged sapience_wrapup call site, confirms sapience-remember.sh's --dry-run already satisfies deliverable (d) functionally but has zero test coverage, and surfaces open plan-level tradeoffs for deliverables (b) and (c).

memory_candidates.content: When auditing an extension's instruction surfaces for 'does X name tool Y as a prescribed write path,' check whether the corpus already has a marker-suppression lint precedent (this codebase's task-reference-patterns.sh / record-version-patterns.sh use a <token>-ok marker to let a legitimate discussing-not-prescribing mention suppress an otherwise-correct grep hit) before building a new mechanized lint from scratch. For a small, static corpus (~12 files), an advisory rules/*.md file stating the contract in prose is proportionate; a new lint is only worth it if the corpus is large or churns often.

A script's own test file name does not guarantee coverage of every sibling script with a related name: scripts/tests/test-sapience-capture.sh (sapience extension) tests only sapience-retrieve.sh despite its generic 'capture' name; sapience-remember.sh (the actual write/capture script) has zero cases there. Before assuming a named test file covers a related script, grep the file for the script's own basename.
